user_reported_bug: there are some scroll issue in template creation flow
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Focused UI verification shows the desktop modal scroll fix works at 1440x800 and the 800px responsive layout is mostly usable, but the template creation flow still has horizontal overflow at mobile/small widths and the required happy-path Submit to Meta flow was not proven successful.

ui_bugs.issue: At 390x844, the modal and CTA button row overflow horizontally: modal right=394.39 on a 390px viewport, modal body scrollWidth=443/clientWidth=374, document scrollWidth=753/clientWidth=390. This violates the small-viewport requirement that everything scrolls without horizontal overflow.

The one allowed happy-path submit attempt with Header=Text, Footer, and Quick replies did not produce an observed POST response within 45 seconds and the modal remained open in the browser session, so the end-to-end submit outcome is not verified as working.

integration_issues.flow: Messages > New template > Submit to Meta
integration_issues.issue: Template submission could not be confirmed from the UI test: no /whatsapp-outreach/templates POST response was captured after clicking Submit to Meta.

issues: The media query collapses the main grid, but does not make the CTA row stack; .rx-tpl-cta-row keeps fixed multi-column sizing.
The modal uses maxWidth: 96vw inside a scrim with 20px padding, which can exceed very narrow viewport width.

action_items: Fix small/mobile viewport horizontal overflow in CreateTemplateModal: account for scrim padding in modal width and stack/narrow fixed rows such as .rx-tpl-cta-row and the top Template name/Category/Language row under 900px or smaller breakpoints.
Retest one clean Submit to Meta happy path and verify a successful POST, success toast, modal close, and resulting local template row. Avoid repeated submissions.
critical_code_review_comments: The added .rx-tpl-body overflow/min-height/flex rules address vertical scrolling on desktop, but the @media (max-width: 900px) block only changes the two-column modal grid and preview stickiness; it does not address nested fixed-width controls that still cause horizontal overflow on narrow screens.
At mobile width, inline maxWidth:'96vw' plus .rx-modal-scrim padding:20px can make the modal exceed the viewport.
seed_data_creation: Used onboarding 'Explore with demo data' once to make the SPA usable; attempted one template name test_scroll_check_<timestamp>, but submission was not confirmed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop checks passed: at 1440x800 with Header=Image and Buttons=CTA, body scrollHeight=906/clientHeight=593, scrollTop moved to 313, header/footer rects stayed fixed, preview top stayed fixed, and window.scrollY remained 0 on overscroll. Responsive 800x700 collapsed to one column and Template name/Buttons were reachable by modal body scroll, though the underlying table page already had horizontal document overflow. Mobile 390x844 still failed with modal/body horizontal overflow. Submit attempt timed out waiting for POST.
rca_of_the_issue: The scroll fix bounded the modal and made the body vertically scrollable, but the responsive rules are incomplete for narrow viewports. The modal width calculation does not account for scrim padding, and nested fixed grids/widths such as .rx-tpl-cta-row continue to exceed the modal body width.
